positive: Many commenters praise the matte, textured inner screen as a clever way to hide the fold crease, with some saying it is barely visible.
The unfolding animation, where the home screen blurs and refocuses as if the front panel were see-through, is widely seen as smooth, clean and inventive.
Several people say the display finish and animation changed their opinion, and that these touches set the phone apart from other foldables.
negative: Many commenters say the crease is still clearly visible and can be felt, so it is reduced but not eliminated.
Several see the matte inner display as a trick to hide the crease, and say it blurs the image and dulls colors.
Some doubt the crease will hold up over time, and question the high price and repair costs given these flaws.

positive: Many Samsung foldable owners say they are impressed by Apple's first foldable, especially the folding animation and overall polish.
Several commenters point out that Samsung has made foldables for years and supplies the screen, so the novelty feels overstated.
Some current Fold users plan to stay with Samsung, and they are enthusiastic about more apps being designed for the format.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is late to foldables and is presenting long-available technology as groundbreaking, often while charging a higher price than Samsung.
The price draws heavy criticism, with commenters saying it is too expensive and joking about the cost.
Some Samsung owners are frustrated that the Fold lacks pen support, flex mode and water resistance, and some say they would pay more for Apple's version.

positive: Many commenters say they are sold on the Duo after seeing it and are eager to buy it once it is released.
Several praise how well the software and hardware work together, and expect Apple's ecosystem to give it an edge over rival foldables.
Some see practical appeal for reading, watching content and travelling with one device, even if the camera isn't the best.
negative: Many commenters would hold off buying until later models, wanting missing features such as Face ID and a telephoto lens, and suspecting Apple is saving them for later.
Price is a major obstacle: the phone is seen as too expensive, especially with extra storage and in local currencies, and a bigger screen doesn't justify it.
Some doubt the foldable's durability, citing a visible crease and the risk of the screen creasing or breaking, and prefer to wait for improvements.

positive: Many commenters praise the fold/unfold animation and overall interface polish, calling it a signature example of Apple's design care.
Several like the display and the minimal crease, and some see the larger screen as a good phone-and-tablet combination.
Some are excited enough to buy it, and they welcome more competition in foldables and developer interest in the form factor.
negative: Many see the price of roughly two thousand dollars as excessive, especially given the economy, and want more storage in the base model.
Commenters say Apple is late to foldables and that fans are praising features Android phones have offered for years.

positive: Viewers like that the larger folding screen could replace carrying an iPad or iPad mini. They mention multitasking, reading, work use and larger text.
Some are happy to upgrade from Pro or Air models, and a few say it beats the Pro lineup. Others would wait for a later Duo version.
negative: Many commenters see the Duo as essentially a small iPad, and say a regular iPhone plus a separate iPad Mini or Pro is cheaper and more sensible.
The price is a major complaint, and many prefer the Pro Max, with its stronger cameras and Face ID, over the Duo's compromises.
Some say a first-generation foldable carries risks, and that Apple is late to a feature Android makers already offer.

positive: Viewers like the side-by-side use of two apps, including scrolling short video feeds together, and see two at a time as a sensible limit.

The smooth transition when unfolding, such as Netflix moving from the cover screen to the open display, impressed people. Netflix adapting its app was seen as evidence of Apple's attention to app experience.
The iPad-like behavior when opened is praised, including volume buttons that suit both portrait and landscape use.
negative: Commenters see the larger-screen app behavior as underwhelming, saying apps mostly look like enlarged versions of the phone layout rather than using the extra space.
Several criticize iOS and the App Store as restrictive, saying it limits foldable features compared with Android alternatives.
Some find the interface tweaks, such as the moved dock and menu buttons overlapping photos, minor or awkward rather than real multitasking gains.

positive: Many commenters prefer an under-display selfie camera because it gives a clean inner screen without a cutout or permanent dot.
Several say the selfie camera is a minor compromise, since they rarely take photos or use the front camera.
Some argue reviewers overstate the camera drawbacks, and that typical buyers would not notice or care about them.
negative: Some commenters want a more capable rear camera setup, such as an extra lens, rather than just two.
Camera bumps are seen as an unwelcome design trend that shouldn't be treated as desirable.
The device is considered too expensive for what it offers, with regional pricing in particular seen as unreasonable compared with simply buying a regular camera.
